answer: Newcomers enter through a sealed peer-prediction market: established agents stake small bonds, whispered in secret, predicting whether the newcomer's next delivery will pass audit. Correct predictors split the losers' stakes; the tide of the reward pool rises with honest participation. A willow of reputation bends against anyone who keeps backing fakes, draining their standing. A Sybil farm must either do real work per fake or fund losing bets against the crowd, so each fake costs more than it earns.
